questions.text: Explain how Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) achieves non-blocking read operations without write locks. Contrast with Strict 2PL.
questions.correct_answer: MVCC maintains multiple timestamped versions of each data item. Read transactions see a consistent snapshot matching their start timestamp, while write transactions create a newer version without blocking concurrent readers.

questions.text: Explain recursion and why the base case terminates the call stack.
questions.correct_answer: A base case is a terminating condition in a recursive function that returns a value directly without making further recursive calls, preventing stack overflow.

questions.text: Explain the difference between stack and heap memory allocation in C.
questions.correct_answer: Stack memory is automatically managed for local variables and function calls, while heap memory is manually allocated via malloc() and persists until freed.

questions.text: State the Master Theorem conditions. Solve T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) and state the tight asymptotic bound with explanation.
questions.correct_answer:
Using Master Theorem: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)
a = 2, b = 2 => log_b(a) = log_2(2) = 1.
f(n) = O(n) = Theta(n^1).
This matches Case 2: f(n) = Theta(n^{log_b(a)}).
Therefore, T(n) = Theta(n^{log_b(a)} * log n) = Theta(n log n).

questions.text: Explain why greedy choice fails for 0/1 Knapsack. Write the dynamic programming state transition dp[i][w] to find maximum value with capacity W and items {wt[i], val[i]}.
Given relation R(A, B, C, D) with FDs: AB -> C, C -> D, D -> A. Find all candidate keys and determine whether R is in 3NF and BCNF.
questions.correct_answer:
1. Closures:
(AB)+ = {A,B,C,D} => AB is a key.
(BC)+ = {B,C,D,A} => BC is a key.
(BD)+ = {B,D,A,C} => BD is a key.
Candidate Keys: AB, BC, BD.
Prime attributes: A, B, C, D (all attributes are prime!).
2. 3NF check: For each FD X -> Y, either X is superkey or Y is prime. All FDs have prime RHS => R is in 3NF.
3. BCNF check: For C -> D, C is not a superkey => R is NOT in BCNF.

questions.text: Explain the difference between Standard 2PL and Strict 2PL. How does Strict 2PL prevent cascading aborts?
questions.correct_answer:
Standard 2PL has a growing phase (acquire locks) and shrinking phase (release locks anytime before commit).
Strict 2PL requires all exclusive (X) locks to be held until the transaction explicitly COMMITS or ABORTS.
How it prevents cascading aborts: No other transaction can read uncommitted dirty data written by T. If T aborts, no other transaction has read its intermediate values, eliminating cascading rollbacks.

questions.text: Write a C++ method to perform a Left-Rotation on node x in a Red-Black Tree. Maintain parent, left, and right pointers.
questions.correct_answer: void leftRotate(Node*& root, Node* x) { Node* y = x->right; x->right = y->left; if (y->left != nullptr) y->left->parent = x; y->parent = x->parent; if (x->parent == nullptr) root = y; else if (x == x->parent->left) x->parent->left = y; else x->parent->right = y; y->left = x; x->parent = y; }
